card.name: Small words after 'is' defining a condition
card.fires_on: The small word right after 'is' or 'are' (not, a, an) when a disease or condition has just been named and is being defined or described. It is common in explanations of what a disorder is or is not.

modes.label: Negation of a cause
modes.description: 'not' after 'is' or 'are' stating what a genetic or skin condition is not, such as inherited or contagious.
modes.example: KS is a genetic condition but it is<< not>> 'inherited' from your parents.

modes.label: Article in a definition
modes.description: 'a' or 'an' after a named condition and 'is', starting a description of the condition.
modes.example: PML is<< an>> opportunistic viral infection of the brain caused

card.writes: It seems to push toward words that describe a condition's nature and away from words about what causes it.
card.plain: It fires on the little word after 'is' when a disease has just been named and the text starts defining it.
